name: Shammah
overview: Shammah was a male warrior known as the Hararite and counted as the twenty-fifth member of "the thirty," a select group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture. There are no additional notes about his life or character beyond his distinguished military role.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammah means "waste" in Hebrew, while another form of his name, Shagee, means "wanderer" or "meanderer like grazing sheep." Neither name was given by God, but they provide insight into the Hebrew naming conventions of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Shammah beyond what is indicated in his unique military designation. There are no known relatives or connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shammah's significance lies in his inclusion among David's elite warriors, "the thirty," highlighting his valor and loyalty in the service of Israel's king. As the Hararite, he represents the diverse group of men who supported David's rise and reign, contributing to the establishment of God's kingdom through faithful military service.
